text:
mira: heads-up — we've seen streaming clients drop after ~10s when using service-account JWT flow. no obvious stack trace, just `ERR_STREAM_CLOSED` on the client. anyone seen this with oidc exchange + streaming? :thinking:

ben: hmm, are you minting a signed JWT and exchanging for an access token, or using workload identity federation?

mira: signed JWT -> exchange. flow: client creates SA JWT (exp 60s), calls our token-exchange endpoint, gets back short-lived access token, then opens stream. sometimes token-exchange returns 400 "invalid_audience" and stream fails to start; other times stream starts then dies after first chunk.

alex: similar to a bug we hit — if the JWT `aud` is the token-exchange URL vs the resource server, the exchange fails intermittently. OIDC bridges we use expect `target_audience` (or audience set to the resource) not the raw exchange endpoint.

mira: interesting. our code sets `aud` to `https://token-exchange.redwood.local` because that's the endpoint receiving the JWT. sample payload we send:

```
{
  "iss": "svc-account@example.com",
  "sub": "svc-account@example.com",
  "aud": "https://token-exchange.redwood.local",
  "exp": 1690000000
}
```

ciara: that will break some federated exchangers. try setting `aud` to the final resource (the API audience) and include `client_id`/`target_audience` in the HTTP form to the exchanger. for example: `aud`: `https://api.redwood.com/.default` or whatever the resource expects.

ben: also check token lifetime alignment — streaming clients expect token TTL >= 30s because we do prefix prefetching. if exchange gives you 20s left, client may open stream then reconnect quickly and hit our rate-limited retry path -> stream closed.

mira: good point. current JWT exp is 60s from creation, but by the time it reaches exchanger and we mint access token, only ~40s left. what do you recommend? bump SA JWT TTL?

alex: we standardize on short SA JWTs (<=5m) but ensure minted access token TTL is >=60s for streaming usage. If your exchanger supports `requested_token_lifetime` include it in the exchange request. Also add jittered backoff on stream reconnects.

mira: quick Q: does the SDK auto-refresh tokens mid-stream or only on open? our Node SDK will refresh the token in the background for non-streaming calls but streams are a single connection.

ciara: SDK currently: it attaches the access token at connection time. we only do refresh on 401 frames. For streaming we rely on the server to accept token rotation via a `token_update` control frame (not all servers support it). If your server doesn't, you need longer TTLs or re-open with exponential backoff.

mira: aha — our server doesn't support token_update yet. that explains the abrupt drop when token runs low. plan: bump requested access TTL to 90s, add jittered reconnect with cap 30s, and ensure `aud` targets resource.

ben: safe defaults to add in SDK: when using SA flow, if detected streaming mode, request min_token_ttl=90 and emit a warning when returned ttl < 60. we can add that in next patch.

alex: also add a small doc note about `aud` vs `target_audience` for the exchange — it's a common pitfall. maybe a snippet: 

```
// create SA JWT with aud = "https://api.redwood.com/" (resource)
// POST to /token-exchange
// form: { grant_type: "urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange", subject_token: <jwt>, subject_token_type: "urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:jwt", requested_token_type: "urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:access_token", requested_token_lifetime: 90 }
```

ciara: yup. and add retries for transient 400/429 from exchanger with small randomized delay. we saw exchangers return 400 for malformed aud then succeed on retry depending on clock skew. :eyes:

mira: thanks — will try that. i'll push a small repro in a separate thread if i hit the 400 again.

deploy-bot: Automated check: token-exchange service responding OK in us-west-2 (latency 48ms) :thumbsup:

ben: if you want, i can open a quick PR to the SDK with the streaming-SA heuristics. low priority but useful.

mira: please do, that'd be great. tagging you @ben. :party_parrot:
